sources.note: Sec. 4.6 Yarawata (pp. 159-160): phoneme inventory /i u a/, /b t d k g m n l w y/, /b/ final devoicing, [s] allophone of /t/ next to /i/, epenthetic final vowel; nothing on stress. sources.note: Sec. 1.3.3 (p. 6): 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet' (all languages of the study). Yarawata appears only as a village of Ukuriguma UKU (sec. 2.22.24.14, p. 53: 'included into the figures of speakers, but disregarded in any other respect'). Wayapan Group typology (p. 54) segmental only; sec. 2.22.8 (p. 73) Adelbert Range Phylum: 'None of the languages appears to be tonal'. No stress placement statement.

tone.quote: [p. 73] The aim of this section is to point out some of the typological features which are universally or almost universally present in the languages of the phylum. 1) The velar nasal is very common. 2) None of the languages appears to be tonal. [p. 53, 2.22.24.14 Ukuriguma UKU (180)] Villages: Ukuriguma, Yarawata, Kagi. Previously unrecorded and not listed in Z'graggen (1969). ... Ukuriguma is included into the figures of speakers, but disregarded in any other respect. (scanned text layer; spurious intra-word letter spacing removed, wording unchanged)
tone.locator: p. 73, sec. 2.22.8, item 2; scope caveat p. 53, sec. 2.22.24.14 'Ukuriguma UKU (180)'
tone.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone.says: Sec. 2.22.8 'Typological characteristics of the Adelbert Range Phylum' lists as feature 2: 'None of the languages appears to be tonal.' The same sentence is repeated for other phyla (p. 74ff item 6), while Romkun (Ramu) is flagged 'possibly tonal' and, in the 1975 sequel C-38, Biyom and Isabi (Brahman) 'appear to be tonal' -- i.e. Z'graggen did note tone where he heard it, and reports none for the Adelbert Range languages. Stress marking was omitted throughout (sec. 1.3.3, p. 6, already listed…
